To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the power consumption of a piezoelectric control system is a function of: (1) the type, size and number of the piezoceramics; and (2) the control law voltage and frequency.

the power required for active control is proportional to the square of the voltage, inversely proportional to the frequency of the control input signal and inversely proportional to some power of the number of piezoelectrics.

the maximum power consumed by a piezoelectric material is independent of the host structure and is a function of material properties, the number of actuators, and the voltage and excitation frequency of the control signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and experimental verification of a model for predicting the power requirements of piezoelectrical actuators for active vibration control of structures.
predicting the power consumption for active vibration control of structures utilizing surface-bonded, piezoelectric, actuator/sensors.
the power requirements of piezoelectrical actuators for the active control of vibration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the power consumption for active control of structures using surface-bond piezoelectric transducers is a function of: (a) the quantity of piezoelectrical transducers, (b) the frequency of the control voltage signal, (c) the voltage of the control voltage, (d) the type of piezoceramics used, (e) the material properties of the piezoceramic, (f) the capacitance of the piezotransducers, and
the power required by the piezoelectrics to control a structure is a function of: the type and quantity of piezoelectronics, the control algorithm and the control effectiveness.

the power consumption of surface-bonded, piezoelectric, vibration control devices is a function of: (1) the quantity, type, and distribution of the piezoceramic material, (2) the voltage and frequency applied to the piezocermic material, (3) the capacitance of the piezomaterial, and (4) the control law effectiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the power consumption of a piezoelectric system is dependent on the type and quantity of piezoelectrics, the control law output voltage and frequency, the capacitance of the piezoceramic actuators, and the effectiveness of the active control system.
the power consumption of a piezoelectric active control system can be estimated by knowing the type of piezoceramic, its size and location, and the control law output voltage.
piezoelectric power consumption can be predicted using a simple model that accounts for the capacitance nonlinearity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power requirements for a perfectly controlled system can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy using simple analytical methods.

the power requirements for active control can be estimated with a simple model and that the power requirements can be minimized by using a control algorithm with a lower control effectiveness and a control voltage that is as low as possible.
for active vibration control, it is not necessary to measure the dynamics between the actuator and host structure to determine the power consumption of an actuator.
